1) Rule implementation for story file validation: - src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts - JSDoc traceability: - "Rule to validate @story annotation references refer to existing story files" - @story docs/stories/006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.story.md - @req REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION, REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS, etc. - Uses core utilities from src/utils/storyReferenceUtils.ts: normalizeStoryPath, containsPathTraversal, hasValidExtension, enforceProjectBoundary. - Path and security checks: - Rejects absolute paths when allowAbsolutePaths is false via path.isAbsolute + invalidPath. - Detects traversal with containsPathTraversal and rejects paths that escape cwd. - Enforces .story.md extension when requireStoryExtension is true (invalidExtension message). - File existence and boundary logic: - reportExistenceProblems → normalizeStoryPath → getStoryExistence. - handleProjectBoundaryForExistence uses enforceProjectBoundary on all candidates and on matchedPath, reporting invalidPath if all candidates are outside project. - reportExistenceStatus maps existence.status "missing" to fileMissing and "fs-error" to fileAccessError (with detailed error message). - Annotation parsing: - Program() walks context.getSourceCode().getAllComments(). - handleComment() splits comment.value into lines, strips everything before @, and for lines starting with "@story" calls validateStoryPath. - validateStoryPath() extracts the path token from the line and passes it to processStoryPath.
2) File system and path resolution utilities: - src/utils/storyReferenceUtils.ts - JSDoc header: - @story docs/stories/006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.story.md - @req REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION, REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION, REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY. - Path resolution (REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS): - buildStoryCandidates(storyPath, cwd, storyDirs): - If storyPath starts with "./" or "../": candidates = [path.resolve(cwd, storyPath)]. - Else: adds path.resolve(cwd, storyPath) and for each dir in storyDirs adds path.resolve(cwd, dir, basename(storyPath)). - Project boundary validation (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY): - enforceProjectBoundary(candidate, cwd) resolves both paths and checks that normalizedCandidate === normalizedCwd or startsWith(normalizedCwd + path.sep). - Existence & caching (REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION): - fileExistStatusCache: Map. - checkSingleCandidate(): wraps fs.existsSync and fs.statSync in try/catch; returns status "exists", "missing", or "fs-error" and caches result. - getStoryExistence(candidates): returns first "exists" with matchedPath; otherwise, if any "fs-error", returns status "fs-error" with error; else status "missing". - storyExists(): boolean shim over getStoryExistence. - normalizeStoryPath(): builds candidates, calls getStoryExistence, returns { candidates, exists, existence }. - Security helpers (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION): - isAbsolutePath, containsPathTraversal, isTraversalUnsafe. - hasValidExtension(p): enforces '.story.md'.
3) Rule documentation and configuration: - docs/rules/valid-story-reference.md - Header: - "Validates that `@story` annotation references refer to existing `.story.md` files within the project and prevents invalid path usage." - @story docs/stories/006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.story.md - @req REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION, REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION. - Describes exactly the behaviors from the story: - Prevents absolute paths unless explicitly allowed. - Prevents path traversal outside the project directory. - Ensures `.story.md` extension when required. - Resolves candidate locations in configured storyDirectories. - Describes fileMissing, invalidExtension, invalidPath, and fileAccessError diagnostics and how they’re emitted. - Detailed "Boundary & Configuration" section explains candidate generation, boundary enforcement, and when invalidPath vs fileMissing vs fileAccessError are reported. - Options documented: - storyDirectories: string[] (default ["docs/stories", "stories"]). - allowAbsolutePaths: boolean (default false). - requireStoryExtension: boolean (default true). - Examples include valid and invalid @story usages matching the story examples.

when allowAbsolutePaths: true it's valid; when false, same code yields invalidPath. - relaxedExtensionTester: with requireStoryExtension: false, accepts `.md` story under docs/stories without invalidExtension. - Project boundary tests (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY): - projectBoundaryTester: absolute path resolved under a fake outside-project root with allowAbsolutePaths: true and storyDirectories pointing there yields invalidPath. - Additional Jest tests: - Misconfigured storyDirectories outside project cannot validate external files: mocks fs to make an external story exist under /tmp/outside; runRuleOnCode asserts there is at least one diagnostic with messageId === "invalidPath". - StoryDirectories cannot escape project via `../outside-boundary.story.md`, verifying boundary handling. - Error-handling tests (REQ-ERROR-HANDLING): - storyExists returns false and does not throw when fs.existsSync and fs.statSync throw EACCES. - storyExists returns false when fs.statSync throws EIO even if existsSync is true. - Rule reports fileAccessError when fs.statSync throws with existsSync true (EIO); diagnostics filtered for messageId === "fileAccessError" and error text contains "EIO". - Rule reports fileAccessError when fs.existsSync and fs.statSync both throw EACCES; diagnostics filtered for messageId === "fileAccessError" and error text contains "EACCES".

traceability.notes: Story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION is fully implemented. The valid-story-reference ESLint rule enforces that @story annotations reference existing .story.md files, with correct path resolution relative to the project root and configurable storyDirectories. Security requirements are met through rejection of disallowed absolute paths, prevention of path traversal outside the project, and enforcement of file extensions when required. File existence checks are cached and aggregated to satisfy performance requirements. Project-boundary enforcement ensures that even when storyDirectories or paths are misconfigured, external files cannot be treated as valid story references; violations are reported as invalidPath. Filesystem errors (permissions, I/O) are handled gracefully without throwing, and are surfaced as fileAccessError diagnostics with helpful context. Dedicated documentation in docs/rules/valid-story-reference.md explains configuration and behavior, aligned with this story. Tests in tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts explicitly reference this story, cover core functionality, configuration scenarios, boundary conditions, and error handling, and these tests run successfully under Jest. All listed acceptance criteria and technical requirements in the story are satisfied based on concrete implementation and test evidence.
